details:
PART 1: Project Summary

AstroQuest — Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a web-based educational space platform built for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 by Team Astro_W1 from International Islamic University Chittagong (IIUC), Bangladesh. It transforms real NASA data into an interactive mission simulator for young learners — explore planets in 3D, build rockets, launch missions, run a Moon base, take quizzes, and see live NASA feeds, all in one place.

PART 2: Problem & Solution

The problem: NASA data is free and public, but it isn't built for a 10-year-old. Textbook diagrams make space feel distant and abstract. Children rarely get to do space — they only read about it.

Our solution: A web app where every child becomes a Junior Astronaut. They explore planets in 3D, build real rockets, launch missions that can succeed or fail, and learn from the outcomes — with real NASA numbers behind every decision.

PART 3: What We Built

Full Backend Version (complete)

  • ASP.NET Core MVC + SQL Server + Identity authentication
  • 25+ REST API endpoints — planets, cosmic objects, quiz grading, rocket launch validation, mission scoring, leaderboard, NASA proxy, AI chatbot
  • Server-side validation (nothing can be faked from the browser)
  • Admin panel for user and quiz management
  • NASA API key kept server-side (never exposed)
  • Anthropic Claude API integration for the "Ask Astro" chatbot

Frontend-Only Build (demo)

  • Because we couldn't host the backend online during the hackathon, we built a standalone frontend version for the live demo
  • mock-api.js intercepts /api/* calls and runs the same backend rules inside the browser
  • localStorage stores accounts, scores, and progress
  • Runs from a single HTML file — no server, no install needed

PART 4: Pages (16 total)

Home · Solar System (3D) · Deep Space (3D) · Rocket Lab · Landing Site · Mission Budget · NASA Live · Quiz · Research · Library · Datasets · Leaderboard · Login · Register · Profile · Admin

PART 5: Game Mechanics

XP system:

  • +5 for exploring a new world
  • +10 per correct quiz answer
  • +25 for a first successful landing
  • Moon mission score ÷ 2

Ranks: Cadet → Pilot (200 XP) → Commander (500 XP)

5 Badges:

  • 🚀 First Launch
  • 🌕 Moon Landing
  • 🧠 Quiz Ace (100% on a quiz)
  • 🪐 Solar Explorer (visit 8 worlds)
  • 🛰️ Moon Commander (Moon mission ≥ 80%)

PART 6: Datasets Used

Primary data sources:

  • NASA Planetary Fact Sheet — all planet statistics (diameter, gravity, temperature, orbit)
  • NASA Open APIs (api.nasa.gov) — APOD, NeoWs (near-Earth objects), Mars Rover Photos, Image Library
  • NASA EONET — live natural events for the world map
  • ISS Position API — real-time space station tracking

Reference datasets (linked, not loaded):
LRO, Cassini (PDS), Magellan (PDS), Voyager (PDS), SDO, Parker Solar Probe, Juno, Europa Clipper, MESSENGER, MOLA, EPIC/DSCOVR, NASA Earthdata

PART 7: Tech Stack

ASP.NET Core · SQL Server · Identity · three.js · Leaflet · vanilla JS / HTML / CSS · Anthropic Claude API · NASA Open APIs

PART 8: Credits

Built by Team Astro_W1 — IIUC, Chittagong, Bangladesh.

Development assisted by Claude (Anthropic) — used for backend code scaffolding, frontend-only build conversion, and documentation.

Data from NASA (public domain).

PART 9: Note About the Demo

Due to hosting constraints during the hackathon, we were unable to host the ASP.NET backend online. What you see in the live demo is the standalone frontend-only build we created separately for showcase purposes. The full backend code (API, database, authentication) is included in this repository and can be run locally with dotnet run.

Each part is self-contained — you can use them separately in different places (About field, README sections, submission form, pitch slides) or stitch them together. Let me know if you want any part expanded, shortened, or rewritten.
